sections.h2: Caddo or Bossier: which parish bills you
sections.html:
Most Shreveport houses are billed by Caddo Parish, since the city is the Caddo Parish seat. Part of the city extends along the west bank of the Red River into Bossier Parish, though, and a house on that side deals with the Bossier Parish assessor and tax collector instead. Check which parish your parcel is in before you go looking for a bill.

A Shreveport mailing address can also belong to a house in one of the small places outside the city, such as Bethany, Dixie, Keithville or Mira. That can change the tax bill, so read the parcel record instead of trusting the postal name.

The city had 187,593 residents in the 2020 census, and the 2024 estimate is 176,578, below the 1980 high of 206,989. The median home was built in 1973, so many houses are fifty years old or more.

sections.h2: Where to look up or pay your property tax
sections.html:
Both Caddo offices share one building: 501 Texas Street in downtown Shreveport. The Assessor is in Room 102, and the Sheriff's tax division is in Room 101.

OfficeWhat it doesContact
Caddo Parish AssessorValues property, handles homestead exemption filings501 Texas Street, Room 102, 318.226.6704, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. weekdays
Caddo Parish Sheriff, Tax DivisionBills and collects the tax501 Texas Street, Room 101, (318) 675-2170

The Assessor's website offers a free property search by owner name, section, township and range, or subdivision, with GIS maps. A day pass for deeper searches costs $10, and a professional subscription is $35 a month.

The Sheriff's site takes payments online, and online tax payments post the same day until 11:59 p.m. It also has a pre-payment program and links to delinquent properties and sheriff sales.

The deadline is December 31. After that, 1% interest is added for every month the tax sits unpaid. The parish collector mails a bill each December that shows the millages and the total due.

Leave it long enough and the collector can put the house up at a tax sale. The former owner then has three years to buy it back. Three years sounds generous, but interest and costs pile up the whole time, so if a delinquency notice arrives, call the Sheriff's tax division that same week.

For an exact interest or fee figure, ask the office for a payoff instead of estimating one. A written payoff is also what a title company needs for a sale.

sections.h2: How homes are assessed and how to appeal
sections.html:
A Shreveport house is taxed on 10% of its fair market value. The ratios are 15% for commercial property and 25% for public service property. If you think the value is wrong, your recourse is the local Board of Review.

Assessment rolls are generally open to the public from August 15 to September 15. Use those weeks to pull your parcel card and set it beside sales of similar houses near you.

  • Check the square footage, bedroom count and year built on the parcel card.
  • Look for exemptions you may have missed.
  • Ask the Assessor how to file with the Board of Review.

The homestead exemption applies to $7,500 of assessed value, which is $75,000 of fair market value. In Caddo, homeowners can apply for it online through the parcel card on the Assessor's property search. Owners 65 and older should ask the Assessor about the special assessment freeze.

If you are selling, remember that a buyer has to claim the exemption on their own once they own and live in the house. Do not promise a buyer your current bill.

sections.h2: Roof, heat and the age of the house
sections.html:
Shreveport has a humid subtropical climate, and severe thunderstorms, hail, damaging winds and tornadoes are part of spring and summer. About 91 days a year top 90 degrees. That mix is hard on roofs and cooling systems, and buyers' inspectors tend to look first at the roof, the HVAC unit, the plumbing and the electrical panel.

  • Keep roof receipts and any storm claim paperwork.
  • Note the age of your air conditioner.
  • Write down any past leaks so the disclosure you give is accurate.

The western and northern parts of the city are low and close to the river, so a flood-zone check matters more there than for houses on higher ground.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax when you sell
sections.html:
Any unpaid tax comes out of your sale proceeds through the title company. La. R.S. 9:2721 also asks the deed to identify who is responsible for the taxes and where notices should be mailed, a detail people skip when closing is rushed.

Ask the Sheriff for a current payoff before closing day. If the sale falls in November or December, the new bill may already be on its way, so agree in writing who covers the year.

The transfer is made by authentic act or act under private signature, and it reaches third persons only once recorded. A Caddo Parish parcel is recorded with the parish clerk of court.

Ask your closing agent who will carry the act to the clerk and when. Recording on the closing date keeps the public record current and lets the buyer's first bill go to the right address.

sections.h2: What to bring when you call or visit
sections.html:
Both offices work faster when you arrive with the right details. Bring your parcel number or owner name, the address as it appears on your deed, and a photo ID. If you are selling for someone else, bring whatever shows you have authority to act, such as succession papers.

At the Assessor's office, Room 102, ask about the homestead exemption, any special assessment freeze for owners 65 and older, and how to reach the Board of Review. At the Sheriff's tax division, Room 101, ask for a payoff, the status of the current year and whether any earlier year is open.

If you cannot make it downtown, the Assessor's online search and the Sheriff's online payment page cover most routine questions without a trip. Heirs who live out of town can use both from anywhere.

sections.h2: Selling with tax owed: the order of work
sections.html:
A house with a past-due bill can still sell, and the steps are short.

  1. Confirm the parish. A parcel on the Bossier side has a different assessor and collector.
  2. Pull the parcel record from the Assessor's search and check the facts on it.
  3. Get a written payoff from the Sheriff's tax division at 501 Texas Street, Room 101.
  4. Give the payoff to your title company so it can pay the balance from your proceeds.
  5. Record the sale with the Caddo Parish clerk of court.

A cash buyer can close on that same path without waiting for a lender, which helps when a delinquency notice has a date on it.

faqs.q: Is Shreveport in Caddo or Bossier Parish?
faqs.a: Most of Shreveport is in Caddo Parish, which it serves as parish seat. Parts of the city extend into Bossier Parish.

faqs.q: When is Shreveport property tax due?
faqs.a: Property tax is due December 31, and 1% interest per month applies after that. Ask the Caddo Sheriff's tax division for the exact payoff.

faqs.q: How do I pay Caddo Parish property tax?
faqs.a: You can pay online through the Caddo Sheriff's site, where online payments post the same day until 11:59 p.m. You can also visit 501 Texas Street, Room 101.

faqs.q: What is the Louisiana homestead exemption?
faqs.a: The exemption covers $7,500 of assessed value, which is $75,000 of fair market value. Caddo owners can apply through the Assessor's online property search.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Shreveport house if I owe tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid tax is paid out of the sale proceeds, and the title company needs a payoff figure from the Sheriff.
